The exact PoC sets `parser_flags == 0x20ffff20`, which enables both `MD_FLAG_TABLES` and `MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS`, and leaves markdown payload bytes `ff 0d 2d 7c 0d 3e 5b 21 6e 4f 54 65 5d 0a 3e ff`, i.e. lines `\xff`, `-|`, `>[!nOTe]`, and `>\xff`, for project parsing.
Source. The parser context stores the attacker-controlled markdown bytes and the enabled extension flags that govern the later table and admonition decisions.
On the witness's second line `-|`, table parsing is enabled and the underline predicate succeeds, so the line is classified as `MD_LINE_TABLEUNDERLINE` with one column instead of ordinary text.
Processing that underline retypes the current block as a table and mutates the cached previous-line analysis object so `pivot_line->type` becomes `MD_LINE_TABLE` for subsequent lines.

On the next line `>[!nOTe]`, case-insensitive tag matching recognizes `note` and converts the surrounding quote block into an admonition, but the function returns immediately while leaving the caller's `pivot_line` pointer unchanged. The fix for this witness adds `*p_pivot_line = &md_dummy_blank_line;` before returning.

When the following quoted content line `>\xff` is analyzed, the stale cached pivot from step 4 is still `MD_LINE_TABLE` because step 5 never reset it. After consuming the quote container mark, `n_parents == ctx->n_containers`, so the line is misclassified as table continuation even though the current block was already ended before the admonition marker.

Because step 6 made the new line's type equal the stale cached `pivot_line->type` (`MD_LINE_TABLE`), the type-change branch does not repair state. `ctx->current_block` is still `NULL` after the admonition-leading-line fast path, so this path calls `md_start_new_block()` with `line->type == MD_LINE_TABLE`.

Sink. `md_start_new_block()` has cases for HR, headers, code, text, HTML, blank, setext underline, and table underline, but not `MD_LINE_TABLE`. The stale value from step 7 therefore indexes the compiler-generated switch table past `switch.table.md_start_new_block`, matching the ASan global-buffer-overflow read of size 4.
First project-code state materialization of the attacker-controlled markdown bytes and parser flags later used by line analysis.
The admonition-leading-line fast path returns after retyping the quote block but does not reset the caller's `pivot_line`, so the prior table state remains live for the next line.
ASan sink. `md_start_new_block()` switches on `line->type`, but the stale-state path supplies unsupported `MD_LINE_TABLE`, so the compiler-generated switch table is read out of bounds.
